thread:
ana_sells: Heads-up — FastCare POC hitting flaky SSE in their webapp. Streams disconnect every ~6-12s, client logs show partial UTF-8 errors and then immediate reconnects. They’re blocked for demo tomorrow. :grimacing:

fastcare_dev: Repro steps from our QA: open websocket-like SSE, after ~few KB of data we see 'Unexpected end of data' in JS console, then EventSource triggers onerror and auto-reconnect. Happens across Chrome and our Android WebView.

ana_sells: Copying logs from customer (raw):

fastcare_dev: ```
> GET /v1/streams?model=redwood-3-stream HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.ai
> Accept: text/event-stream
> Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>
> 
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
< Transfer-Encoding: chunked
< 
000a
data: {"chunk":"Hello wor"}
0005
data: {"chunk":"ld"}
0003
dat

// then client complains about invalid utf8 sequence
```

luis_devex: Two immediate guesses: proxy buffering / chunk coalescing at infra layer, or our SDK/client treating chunk boundaries as message boundaries. Can you confirm if they go through a load balancer / Cloudflare / nginx?

fastcare_dev: They’re running behind an Nginx reverse proxy + GCP LB. We tried bypassing LB and it improved but still saw partials on Android. Chrome repro seems more frequent behind proxy.

ben_runtime: @fastcare_dev can you pull the server-side request/response logs for the request-id? I want to see send/flush timings. Also which model + streaming mode are you using (tokens vs delta messages)?

fastcare_dev: Model: redwood-3-stream, streaming type: chunked JSON deltas. Request-id: rwd-pc-84d3. Server logs attached (excerpt):

fastcare_dev: ```
[2026-03-19T10:24:12Z] req=rwd-pc-84d3 flush bytes=1024
[2026-03-19T10:24:12Z] req=rwd-pc-84d3 flush bytes=512
[2026-03-19T10:24:13Z] req=rwd-pc-84d3 flush bytes=256
[2026-03-19T10:24:18Z] req=rwd-pc-84d3 connection reset by peer
```

hope_ml: Two possibilities from ML/runtime side: 1) our streaming emitter is flushing mid-codepoint if encoding+chunking are done purely byte-based, rare but possible when combined with intermediate gzip or proxy buffering; 2) client-side decoder expecting event framing in a specific pattern. Try forcing UTF-8 boundaries server-side by using full-message flush or using base64 payload for bytes to be safe.

maya_solns: Quick repro command for the customer to compare raw behavior:
```bash
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=redwood-3-stream"
```
If `curl -N` stays stable but browser errors, likely client/WebView parsing. If curl also breaks, it's infra.

fastcare_dev: Ran curl -N — it shows interleaved partial lines and then a connection close. So infra likely.

luis_devex: Common nginx fix: set `proxy_buffering off; proxy_request_buffering off; chunked_transfer_encoding on;` in the location block, and ensure `proxy_http_version 1.1;` so we preserve chunked streaming semantics. Could you ask them to toggle this in staging?

fastcare_dev: I can patch nginx config in their staging and retest. Will try disabling gzip as well.

ben_runtime: Also check for any intermediate WAF/edge that rewrites Transfer-Encoding or applies body filtering. On our side I'll look for our chunk emitter logic — maybe add an option to coalesce small flushes into fuller messages (server-side buffer up to X bytes or until boundary token). I can push a hotfix toggle to dedicated POC customers.

hope_ml: For an immediate workaround, we can provide an alternate endpoint that wraps payloads with newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) instead of SSE events — clients just parse lines. That avoids SSE parser quirks. Will ask product for toggle.

ana_sells: Pricing/demo impact: customer is concerned about SLAs for demo. Can eng own a short-term patch we can ship today and then a proper fix after?

ben_runtime: I'll cut a small runtime flag to coalesce flushes and enable it for their tenant. Need approval to deploy to POC tier. @deploy-bot any deploy window?

deploy-bot: Scheduled infra deploy window available in 30 minutes — can roll a small config flag to staging first. Use canary=1%.

fastcare_dev: Thanks — we'll stand by. Also we found repeated 429 rate-limit hints right before disconnects in some traces (X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0) — could that cause abrupt closes?

ben_runtime: If the platform returns 429 mid-stream we should send a proper SSE `event: error` + `data:` and then close gracefully. If the LB/edge is dropping the connection due to throttling, that’s upstream. We'll trace the trace-id for 429s.

luis_devex: Action items:
- @fastcare_dev: flip nginx proxy buffering off in staging and run curl + browser test (ETA 1h)
- @ben_runtime: add temporary coalesce flag for POC tenant and prepare canary (ETA 2h)
- @hope_ml: prepare ndjson endpoint proposal (docs + quick toggle)
- @ana_sells: inform customer about temporary mitigations and schedule follow-up demo once staging validated

fastcare_dev: ack — will update here with results.

ana_sells: Appreciate the quick triage. If we can get a staging pass today we can keep demo slot. :pray:

fastcare_dev: Update 45m later — disabling proxy_buffering + gzip on nginx staging fixed the curl repro and browser session looks stable. No more UTF-8 partial errors so far. Will run longer soak.

ben_runtime: Great — I'll still roll the coalesce flag to reduce risk for other customers; follow-up PR linking here when ready.

ana_sells: Customer notified and tentatively keeping demo. Closing loop after soak. :thumbsup:
